scenario: AITA for asking my pregnant SIL to leave the family Christmas gathering? | Okay so based on title I totally sound like an asshole but hear me out. So this year is our turn to host the family Christmas party at our home. We invited not only my SOs side but also my side as well. Overall it was around 20ish people in our home today for gift giving and typical American Christmas celebrating. Drinks were shared, food broken, the whole shebang. Amongst my SOs side of the family was his pregnant sister. She, I think, was due maybe a week or so ago? But really its just been ticking time bomb for her little one to arrive. Everybodys excited to meet the baby! Now our problem is that SIL came to the party with contractions and was obviously in labor (I know this because Im a mom myself - once you know, you know). Every 20 minutes or so she would start having pains and would make noises to pass the contractions. At first it wasnt so bad; I understand how sucky it is and you dont want to go to the hospital too soon because they'll just send you right home. But then it became almost obnoxious. I feel terrible for saying that but it really was. A lot of my family members and some of hers were glancing around like WTF? Go home and do that in private. After a while it became apparent that it was making everybody uncomfortable and even my MIL reccommend that she rest at home before it gets too late. She refused and said she was fine. In the middle of the kids opening their presents she went into pain again and this time she even screamed for a second. I then discreetly pulled her husband to the side and told them to leave. I did it politely ("Hey I appreciate you guys for being here but I think its time to go. I dont want you guys to give birth in our kitchen! lol"). After I said that her husband got angry and quickly got her and the kids packed up. She visibly upset and before heading out called me a bitch and said that I ruined Christmas for her. A few of their sides family members gave me dirty looks and left soon after. Im torn on this: I wanted everybody to have a good day but it was very distracting and obnoxious to have her around. I feel bad but still. tl;dr -- I asked SIL to leave family Christmas party because she was in labor.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it was right or wrong for this person to ask their pregnant sister-in-law to leave the family Christmas gathering. Let me start by understanding the situation better. So, the family was hosting a Christmas party with around 20 people. The sister-in-law (SIL) was pregnant, due any day, and she came to the party while in labor. She was having contractions every 20 minutes and making noises, which made people uncomfortable. The mother of the host (MIL) suggested she rest at home, but she refused. During the kids' present-opening, she screamed in pain, and the host discreetly asked her husband to leave. The SIL got upset, called the host a bitch, and some of her family left too. The host feels bad but also thinks it was distracting and obnoxious. Hmm, so the main issue here is balancing the comfort and enjoyment of the majority of the guests with the needs and situation of the SIL. On one hand, the SIL was in a vulnerable state, in labor, and probably didn't want to leave the gathering. On the other hand, her behavior was making others uncomfortable, disrupting the event, and potentially putting her and her baby at risk. I think it's important to consider the impact of her actions on the rest of the family. If her contractions were so frequent and loud that they distracted from the celebration, it's understandable that the host felt the need to intervene. However, asking someone to leave, especially in such a personal and sensitive situation, is a tough call. Maybe there were alternative ways to handle the situation without asking her to leave. For example, suggesting she take a break in a quiet room, offering support, or contacting medical help if necessary. But given the immediate disruption and the potential risks, the host might have felt it was the only option. I also wonder about the cultural and familial dynamics. In some families, hosting such events is a big deal, and maintaining harmony is crucial. The host's actions might have been seen as rude or insensitive, especially if the SIL felt she was being judged or pushed out. In the end, it's a tough spot to be in. The host wanted everyone to have a good day, but the SIL's situation was causing significant disruption. It's a delicate balance between being considerate of someone's personal struggles and maintaining the well-being of the entire group. I think the host did what they thought was best in the moment, but it's clear that it caused hurt feelings and tension. It might have been better to approach the situation with more empathy and find a compromise that accommodated both the SIL's needs and the family's gathering.
